title: How he learned to improvise
summary: He learned improvising while learning the instrument, hearing changes by ear, as with Red Allen.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Well, let me maybe make a shift in gears here, and ask when you began improvising.
Oh, I think -- when did I begin improvising? I don't know.
Yeah, I don't know. I guess -- I think ... gee, that's hard for me to say.

See, what I'd like to get at in a rather general way is just to have your views on how it is that -- I'm loathe to use the word 'learn' -- to improvise, but for lack of something better, how is it that one learns to improvise?
At least in your case -- not perhaps, to try to get a covering law from you, but how was it do you think, in your case that you learned to improvise?
Well, I think I was learning the instrument at the same time that I was attempting to improvise. You know?

And I was hearing improvisation on records and in some instances, in hearing musicians live, and having fooled around a little with the piano, I kind of could hear, you know, changes, chord structures, a little -- and this is very basic to improvisation, you know, to learn this, or at least be able to hear it, first, you know, even if you can't name all of the chords, which, of course, it helps if you can -- but I know there are many musicians that
at that period, could improvise very well, and still didn't know a C from an F diminished you know. That is, by name. They would know it by sound, but not by name, not necessarily.

Just like -- oh, we'll take a reasonably advanced, well ... not reasonably advanced, but a very advanced musician, like Red Allen. Red Allen would run a diminished change against anything, and make it sound good, you know, because he does it with such authority, and you'd say, oh, I know he you meant that ... and you'd start to think of chord substitution, really, you know -- even though the guitar and the piano were doing something else.
